## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.
     Reference commits and link to plans and notes. Prose beats a checklist here —
     this is the part you will actually reread in three months. -->

- **Read Sam's slides through the Slides API** and tallied characters per font. The family is
  Rubik, not "Rubrik": Rubik 400/600 italic for text, Rubik Microbe for headlines, and Dirt,
  Vinyl, Wet Paint, Pixels and Burned for accents. All are free on Google Fonts.
- **Planned [style typography](../plans/2026-10-02_style-typography.plan.md).** Yan chose Rubik
  for both the app UI and comics, and balloons that follow their style live.
- **Built it.** Each style now sets the lettering for every balloon type (family, weight,
  italic, capitals) in a `style_profiles.typography` column.
  - A balloon with no font of its own follows its style.
  - The old Comic Neue and Bangers stamps count as unset, so existing comics move onto Rubik
    with no document migration.
  - The house default is Rubik, with italic capitals for captions, after the slides' narration,
    and Rubik Microbe for SFX.
  - The Inspector font menu has a "Style — …" option; there is a Typography section on the
    style page; the app UI is in Rubik with a Microbe wordmark.
- **Rubik is wider than the system font,** so the editor toolbar clipped at 1440px. Its icon
  buttons now show icons only below 2xl.
- **Tests:** unit 334, integration 34 and e2e 24, all green.
- **Shipped** (7bfcabc): the migration went to production, then Yan ran `vercel deploy --prod`.
- **Checked the live comics in the browser** by measuring text against its box. Production is
  all Rubik. Of 81 balloons, 8 now overflow:
  - **6 speech balloons and captions** (Youngest Delegate p1 ×2, p4 ×2; Year It Snowed p2–p4)
    run 5–35px too tall, because Rubik is wider than Comic Neue.
  - **2 SFX** (BEEP BOOP, FSSSSHH) run about 40px too wide, because Rubik Microbe is much wider
    than Bangers.
  - Waiting on Yan: refit those balloons, or change the defaults.
- **Font menus that preview each font.** Yan wants SFX to choose freely among Rubik Dirt,
  Microbe and the other cuts, picked by eye as in Slides. Built `FontPicker`, a keyboard listbox
  that draws each name in its own face, for the Inspector and the style page.
  - Two fixes along the way: a space typed mid-name had picked the font early, and the
    Inspector's list was wider than its panel and got clipped.
  - **Fixed a test race.** `styles.e2e` and the new typography test both assumed their style was
    first in the team-wide list, so run in parallel they picked each other's. Both now press ↓
    until their own style is checked (`e2e/support/styles.ts`).
  - **Ran the tests in a clean worktree** (HEAD plus only these changes), because the A1-board
    session was editing the same tree. There, `auth`, `collab`, `mcp` and `share` fail on HEAD's
    A1 change (new comics have 16 panels, not 12). Not from this work.
- **Story paneling, *The Youngest Delegate* (Khai's chapter).** Drafted 7-page dialogue, then
  set it aside for paneling. Read the geometry of Sam's slides: an A1 board, a 350 pt header, a
  1684 pt square of comic and a 350 pt footer. At a reading distance of 1–1.5 m the square reads
  like a hand-held comic page, so it holds 7–9 panels on a 4×4 grid and 80–120 words. Proposed 54
  panels over 7 pages, one per Edited Drafts scene. Yan put the story in **Act Two, "Taming
  Currents"**, and pinned the story work until the app supports the board.
- **Planned the [A1 board format](../plans/2026-10-02_a1-board-format.plan.md):** a square grid
  between a header and a footer, comic-wide defaults with per-page overrides, and balloons that
  escape the grid.
- **Built the A1 board** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_a1-board-format.plan.md)). New comics are
  1000 × 1416 boards: a 4 × 4 grid in the 1000 × 1000 square between a 208-unit header and footer.
  The header and footer have comic-wide defaults that each page can override, in the Inspector
  and over MCP (`set_header_footer`). Balloons already lived on the page, so they cross panel
  borders and the bands with no change. Checked in Chrome against local Supabase: header editing,
  Use on every page, Tab order (header → panels → footer), a caption straddling a border, a
  balloon in the footer, and an A1 `@page` for PDF. That check found new balloons landing on the
  header title; fixed so they start inside the grid. Unit tests: 366.
- **Another session was editing the same checkout** (the font picker for style typography). I
  committed only my own hunks of `Inspector.svelte`, and checked my commits in a clean worktree.
  GitHub had nothing new to pull.
- **Balloon design** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_balloon-design.plan.md)), from the three
  `speech_bubble-inspo` moodboard photos. Five additions:
  - **Roundness**, from an exact ellipse to a box; tails attach to whatever outline it makes.
  - **Counts** for cloud bumps and shout spikes, plus a spike depth.
  - **Corner anchors**: the balloon is cut off flush by the panel border, which stays whole over
    it, and it follows the corner when the grid changes.
  - **Connected balloons**: a neck that merges the two outlines, or a thin line.
  - **Strikethrough** in balloon text.

  Yan chose the flush trim, and necks as the default with the line as the option. Checking in
  Chrome found two fixes: Inspector edits now re-seat an anchored balloon, and a connector meets
  a clipped balloon where it shows. Unit tests: 405. Open: a neck between balloons in different
  panels crosses the gutter.
- **A QR code to riverbanks.lol in every board footer** ([plan](../plans/2026-10-02_footer-qr.plan.md)),
  about 89 mm on A1, with the address under it and a live link in the PDF. It is editable per
  page like the other footer slots. Chrome's BarcodeDetector decoded the rendered code as
  https://riverbanks.lol; a phone scan of a printed board is still to do.
